c.tagline: Sun-bleached Indian Ocean capital of Afro-Latin rhythm and colonial grandeur.

taxi.color: white with a colored stripe (often blue/green)
taxi.fareNote: Most taxis lack working meters; agree the fare in cash before departing, or use a rideshare app like Yango where available.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; many visitors call hotel/embassy contacts or private medical services (e.g. Clinica Cruz Azul) directly for serious issues.

hood_landmark.Costa do Sol: Costa do Sol Restaurant, Avenida Marginal, Maputo

avoid.reason: Petty crime and bag-snatching; caution at night; police shakedowns — carry ID copies

hood_desc: Polana (Cimento), the leafy, embassy-lined heart of the city with tree-shaded avenues, upscale hotels and restaurants; best for first-time visitors wanting comfort and easy walking to sights.
Sommerschield, a quiet residential and diplomatic quarter next to Polana with guesthouses and boutique stays; suits business travelers and those wanting a calmer base near embassies.

Baixa (city centre/downtown), the historic colonial core near the port and train station with markets, museums and budget-to-midrange lodging; suits travelers who want to walk to landmarks and nightlife.
Costa do Sol, the breezy Marginal beachfront strip northeast of downtown known for seafood restaurants and sea views; suits travelers who want a relaxed, scenic base near the water.
Malhangalene, a mixed local residential and commercial neighborhood with more affordable guesthouses; suits budget travelers wanting an authentic, less touristy feel close to the center.

water.note: Tap water is not recommended for visitors; use bottled or treated water.

transit.pay: Bus and chapa fares are paid in cash (small metical notes/coins) directly to the driver or conductor on board; there is no citywide contactless fare card. Have exact change ready, as chapas are informal and crowded.
transit.hours: Buses and chapas run roughly 5:00-21:00; service thins out after dark and few options run late night, so taxis or rideshare are recommended after dusk.
transit.note: Public transport is crowded, informal and best suited to confident travelers; most visitors rely on taxis, hotel transfers, or the Yango app for convenience and safety.

train: CFM commuter rail to Machava/Matola (limited tourist use)
Sitting service toward Ressano Garcia (South Africa border)
bus: Intercape/long-distance coaches to Johannesburg and regional cities
ferry: Small passenger boats/dhows across Maputo Bay to Catembe (largely superseded by the Maputo-Katembe Bridge)

tip.r: Not obligatory but appreciated; round up taxi fares and leave ~10% at sit-down restaurants where a service charge isn't already included.

food.name: Camarao grelhado a peri-peri (peri-peri prawns)
food.desc: Big Indian Ocean prawns split, charred over coals and painted with fiery peri-peri, garlic and lemon butter. Maputo's defining plate.

places.name: Restaurante Costa do Sol
places.note: 1930s beachfront institution; the classic address for peri-peri prawns and sunset beers.

places.name: Mercado do Peixe (Fish Market)
places.note: Buy prawns by the kilo at the stalls, pay a nearby cook to grill them peri-peri style.

places.name: Zambi
places.note: Polished seafood house over Maputo Bay, praised for very fresh prawns and crab.

food.name: Matapa
food.desc: Young cassava leaves pounded with peanuts, coconut milk and garlic, often with prawns or crab, ladled over rice or xima cornmeal.

places.name: Mamma Mia
places.note: Popular garden restaurant where the matapa and crab curry outshine the pizzas.

places.name: Zambi
places.note: Does a refined matapa com camarao alongside the grilled seafood menu.

places.name: Mercado Municipal food stalls
places.note: Cheap home-style matapa served at lunchtime by cooks in the market's hot-food corner.

food.name: Frango a Zambeziana
food.desc: Chicken marinated in fresh coconut milk, garlic, lime and piri-piri, then grilled slowly over charcoal until lacquered. A Zambezia classic.

places.name: Piri Piri
places.note: Long-running grill house that built its name on coconut-and-chilli chicken.

places.name: Cantina 200
places.note: Cheap, busy local canteen doing charcoal peri-peri chicken and rice at low prices.

places.name: Restaurante Costa do Sol
places.note: Reliable Zambeziana chicken if you want it with a sea view and old-school service.

food.name: Prego no pao and pao com chourico
food.desc: Portuguese-legacy snacks: garlicky steak or spicy sausage stuffed into a crusty pazinho roll, eaten standing at a cafe counter.

places.name: Cafe Continental
places.note: Art-deco Maputo landmark; pregos, pastries and strong coffee among old-city regulars.

places.name: Mercado Janet
places.note: Neighbourhood market with bakery stalls turning out fresh rolls and filled pregos.

places.name: Mercado Municipal bakeries
places.note: Morning bread counters inside the 1901 market; cheapest way to try pazinho fresh.

food.name: Caranguejo e peixe grelhado (crab and grilled fish)
food.desc: Mud crab in coconut curry or whole reef fish grilled with lemon and piri-piri, usually with xima, rice or matapa on the side.

places.name: Mercado do Peixe
places.note: Pick your own crab and fish from the ice, then have it cooked to order alongside.

places.name: Campo di Mare
places.note: Waterfront seafood spot regularly named for fresh fish and bay views.

places.name: Mamma Mia
places.note: Its crab curry is a local favourite and cheaper than the Marginal seafood houses.

food.name: Chamussas and badjias
food.desc: Indian-influenced street snacks: crisp beef or vegetable samosas and spiced split-pea fritters sold hot in paper cones with chilli sauce.

places.name: Mercado Municipal
places.note: Snack vendors ring the market; best selection mid-morning when batches come out.

places.name: Mercado Janet
places.note: Neighbourhood favourite for fresh badjias and chamussas at a few meticais each.

places.name: Feira de Artesanato (Saturday craft market)
places.note: Weekend stalls sell chamussas and grilled snacks alongside the crafts.

food.name: 2M and Laurentina beer
food.desc: Mozambique's two big lagers: crisp 2M and the maltier Laurentina Preta dark, both drunk ice-cold with grilled prawns or chicken.

places.name: Nucleo de Arte
places.note: Artists' collective with a leafy bar; cold beers, live music and a mixed local crowd.

places.name: Dhow
places.note: Stylish bar-restaurant with art on the walls, good for a beer before dinner.

places.name: Restaurante Costa do Sol
places.note: Beachfront terrace where a cold 2M with prawns is the standard Maputo Sunday.

food.name: Tipo Tinto rum with raspberry (R&R)
food.desc: Maputo's unofficial house drink: harsh local Tipo Tinto rum cut with raspberry Sparletta soda over ice. Also try cashew feni-style aguardente.

places.name: Coconuts Live
places.note: Big late-night bar and club where R&R is poured by the jug.

places.name: Mundo's
places.note: Expat-and-local pub with a long terrace, cocktails and screens for football.

places.name: Nucleo de Arte
places.note: Relaxed, unpretentious spot for rum-and-raspberry with a local crowd.

landmarks: Maputo Central Railway Station
A grand Beaux-Arts building with a vast green dome, often linked to Gustave Eiffel's design firm and considered one of Africa's most beautiful train stations.
Casa de Ferro (Iron House)
A striking prefabricated cast-iron building believed to be designed by Gustave Eiffel's studio, a quirky must-photograph piece of colonial-era engineering.
Cathedral of Our Lady of Conception
A soaring white modernist Catholic cathedral in central Maputo whose clean geometric lines make it a striking architectural landmark.
Maputo Fortress (Fortaleza de Nossa Senhora da Conceição)
A red 19th-century fort overlooking the bay, packed with cannons and colonial history right in the heart of the city.
Tunduru Botanical Gardens
A lush, English-designed 19th-century garden of towering baobabs and exotic trees offering a green escape in the city center.
Maputo City Hall (Conselho Municipal)
An imposing neoclassical building anchoring Praça da Independência, one of the city's most photographed civic facades.
Maputo Municipal Market (Mercado Municipal)
A bustling early-1900s market hall bursting with color, spices, and seafood that captures everyday Maputo life.
Hotel Polana (Polana Serena)
An elegant 1922 colonial-era grand hotel perched above the bay, an iconic symbol of Maputo's old-world glamour.
Natural History Museum
A charming Art Nouveau building famous for its collection of preserved elephant fetuses and taxidermy, a quirky architectural and cultural gem.
Maputo Bay Waterfront
The scenic curve of coastline along Avenida Marginal, popular for sunset views, palm-lined promenades, and seaside photography.

train.note: CFM runs a basic daily domestic commuter train from Maputo up to Ressano Garcia on the South African border. The cross-border passenger train to Komatipoort/Johannesburg has been suspended for years, as has the weekly Maputo-Bulawayo (Zimbabwe) service - cross into South Africa by bus instead.

bus.note: Intercape coaches leave Maputo for Johannesburg and Pretoria via the Ressano Garcia-Lebombo border (carry your passport). Local minibuses (chapas) also run to the border and on to Nelspruit.

ferry.note: No international ferries. Small local boats serve Inhaca Island in Maputo Bay; the old Maputo-Catembe crossing is now largely replaced by the Maputo-Katembe suspension bridge.

half.name: Catembe
half.blurb: A short ferry across the bay rewards you with fresh seafood and skyline views.

half.name: Macaneta
half.blurb: Wild dune-backed beaches and a peaceful lagoon make this a popular coastal escape.

half.name: Maputo Special Reserve
half.blurb: Spot elephants, antelope and pristine coast in this restored wilderness south of the city.

half.name: Bilene
half.blurb: A calm saltwater lagoon town beloved for swimming, watersports and easygoing beach days.

full.name: Inhaca Island
full.blurb: This tropical island across the bay offers coral reefs, snorkeling and quiet beaches.

full.name: Kruger National Park
full.blurb: Cross the border for world-class safari and Africa's iconic Big Five wildlife.
